title: Annotating Very High-Resolution Satellite Imagery: A Whale Case Study
author: Cubaynes, Clarke, et al.

steps.title: Acquire VHR Satellite Imagery
steps.instruction: Obtain very high-resolution (VHR) satellite imagery from commercial operators such as Airbus, Maxar Technologies, or Planet.

substeps.instruction: Choose between panchromatic images (single band, greyscale, highest resolution) or multispectral images (multi-band, colored, lower resolution). Note: WorldView-1 only captures panchromatic images.
Decide between requesting custom tasking for a specific time/location or purchasing more affordable archival imagery.

Reference specific satellite resolutions if needed: Pleiades (0.5m), Pleiades Neo (0.3m), GeoEye-1 (0.41m), Ikonos-2 (0.82m), Quickbird-2 (0.65m), WorldView-1 (0.50m), WorldView-2 (0.46m), WorldView-3 (0.31m), WorldView-4 (0.31m), WorldView-Legion (0.31m), SkySat (0.5m), or Pelican (0.3m).

steps.title: Pre-process Imagery
steps.instruction: Perform necessary pre-processing based on the acquired product type and survey goals.

substeps.instruction: Determine if images need to be projected or pansharpened based on the provider's product names (e.g., Airbus Primary/Projected/Ortho; Maxar System-Ready/View-Ready/Map-Ready; Planet SkySat Basic/Ortho Scene/Ortho Collect).
Apply corrections for the top of the atmosphere if required by the survey goals.

steps.title: Perform Systematic Scanning
steps.instruction: Review the entire image for cetaceans using a systematic grid-based scanning pattern (top to bottom, alternating left-to-right and right-to-left).

substeps.instruction: Set the review scale based on animal size: 1:1250 for small cetaceans (< 9m), 1:1500 for large cetaceans (9-20m), and 1:2000 for very large species (> 25m, e.g., fin or blue whales).
Zoom in as needed for detailed inspection.
Track reviewed grid cells to manage large areas (e.g., > 500km²).

steps.title: Annotate Detections
steps.instruction: Label detected whales by placing points or bounding boxes and recording metadata in an attribute table (e.g., using ESRI ArcMap or ArcGIS Pro shapefiles).

substeps.instruction: Record essential image metadata: Observer, location, Satellite, Ground sampling distance (found in panchromatic file Properties > Source > Raster Information), Image ID, Image date, Image time, Product type, Geographical coordinate system, and Projection.
Assess environmental conditions: Sea state (1=Good to 5=Poor), Cloud coverage (0=SKC to 8=OVC), Cloud thickness (1=Thin to 4=Mix), Glare (0=None to 3=Severe), and Turbidity (1=Non-turbid to 4=Mix).
Assign species identification and certainty levels: 1=Definite (90-100%), 2=Probable (60-90%), or 3=Possible (10-60%).

Document morphological and behavioral traits: Body color, Body shape, Body length, Body width, Flipper, Long flipper, Fluke, Head callosities, White lower jaw, After breach, Bubble net, Contour, Flukeprint, Wake, Blow, Mudtrail, Surface active group, Travel group, Mother-calf pair, Other group, and Defecation.

steps.title: Create Bounding Boxes
steps.instruction: Generate bounding boxes for machine learning training using the point shapefiles and associated metadata.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the bounding box is at least twice the size of the known adult size for the target species.

steps.title: Generate Image Chips
steps.instruction: Clip the satellite image into individual image chips using the bounding boxes.

substeps.instruction: Verify licensing restrictions with the satellite provider regarding the sharing of raw images or subsets (e.g., png or jpeg formats).
